Full-time Roof Plumber position available with competitive salary. Work in a dynamic team in Sydney area, NSW. 

3 Stand-out Bullet Points:

•	Full-Time Roof Plumber
•	Salary Range: $75,000 - $95,000 per annum plus superannuation
•	Exciting opportunity to work in a professional setting.

About Us
Austek Roofing & Cladding is a premier provider of specialised metal roofing and wall cladding solutions, serving the Sydney Metropolitan, Greater Sydney, and regional NSW markets. With many years of collective industry experience, we have built a reputation for delivering exceptional quality, unparalleled safety, and lasting durability on projects of all scales—from large-scale industrial warehouses and commercial complexes to bespoke architectural residences

About the role
Roof Plumber installs, maintains, and repairs flashings, metallic roof and wall claddings, and rainwater products such as gutters and downpipes. The successful candidate will be responsible for ensuring all roofing and cladding work is completed to the highest standards of quality, safety, and compliance with Australian building codes and project specifications.

Duties and Responsibilities

• Studying and interpreting blueprints, drawings, and specifications to determine the layout of roof plumbing systems and the materials required.
• Selecting and assessing materials and equipment for each project to ensure they meet specifications and quality standards.
• Measuring, cutting, shaping, and fitting metal sheets and components to fabricate metal roofing, wall cladding, flashings, and rainwater goods.
• Installing metal roof and wall cladding systems on commercial, industrial, and residential buildings.
• Installing, repairing, and maintaining gutters, downpipes, rainwater heads, and other rainwater collection and disposal systems to ensure effective drainage.
• Fabricating and installing roof flashings around vents, chimneys, skylights, and other penetrations to create a watertight seal.
• Sealing joints and seams using techniques such as soldering, brazing, riveting, or applying high-performance sealants.
• Conducting inspections and tests on installed systems to ensure they are secure, watertight, and compliant with all relevant building codes, Australian Standards, and manufacturer's guidelines.
• Identifying and rectifying leaks or defects in roofing systems and rainwater products.
• Adhering strictly to all workplace health and safety (WHS) regulations, including working safely at heights, using personal protective equipment (PPE), and maintaining a safe work environment.
• Coordinating work with other trades on construction sites to ensure projects are completed efficiently and on schedule.
• Maintaining tools and equipment in a safe and operational condition.

Essential Skills

•	Meticulous and precise in all aspects of work to ensure high-quality, watertight installations.
•	Ability to identify issues, assess options, and implement effective solutions on-site.
•	Capable of performing physically demanding tasks, including lifting heavy materials, climbing ladders, and working at heights in various weather conditions.
•	A strong and demonstrable commitment to maintaining a safe work environment for oneself and others.
•	Ability to work effectively as part of a team and communicate clearly with supervisors, colleagues, and other trades.
•	Punctual, dependable, and possessing a strong work ethic.
•	Skilled in the use of hand and power tools specific to the roof plumbing trade.
•	General Construction Induction Card (White Card).

Qualifications needed:

•	Relevant certificate qualification or equivalent relevant work experience
•	Minimum one year of work experience on relevant position

What We Offer

•	Competitive salary based on experience
•	Opportunities for professional growth and training
•	A supportive and dynamic work environment
•	Work on exciting projects with cutting-edge technology

Salary:  The role offers a remuneration package ranging from $75,000-$95,000 plus superannuation for a 38-hour work week.

How to Apply: 11 Recruitment is your pathway to securing this exciting opportunity. We are looking forward to facilitating your application and potentially welcoming you to a company that values expertise. Apply now and let us help you take the next step in your career.

result.description:
Full-time Bricklayer (Blocklayer) position available with competitive salary. Work in a dynamic team in Carlisle WA 6101. 

3 Stand-out Bullet Points:
•	Full-Time Bricklayer (Blocklayer)
•	Salary Range: $75,000 - $95,000 per annum plus superannuation
•	Exciting opportunity to work in a professional setting.

About Us
Monolith Civil Australia is a premier civil construction and infrastructure contractor. We deliver large-scale commercial, industrial, and public infrastructure projects across Australia. We are committed to safety, structural integrity, and operational excellence. Our teams work on complex civil engineering projects requiring high-quality masonry, blockwork, and structural bricklaying.

About the role
The Bricklayer (Blocklayer) is responsible for constructing, repairing, and maintaining brick, block, and stone structures across various civil construction sites. This role requires precision in laying materials for retaining walls, structural foundations, and infrastructure components. The successful candidate will interpret architectural plans, calculate material requirements, and execute masonry work to strict Australian Standards and project specifications.

Duties and Responsibilities

•	Study blueprints, civil engineering drawings, and specifications to determine material requirements, dimensions, and installation procedures.
•	Seal foundations with damp-resistant materials to prevent moisture ingress.
•	Prepare mortar mixtures to correct consistencies and spread mortar accurately for structural integrity.
•	Lay bricks, stone, structural tiles, and heavy concrete building blocks in specified rows, designs, and shapes.
•	Check the vertical and horizontal alignment of structures continuously using plumb bobs, spirit levels, and laser levels.
•	Cut, shape, and polish stones, bricks, and blocks using specialized masonry saws and hand tools to fit custom spaces.
•	Build retaining walls, structural pillars, manholes, and other masonry components required for civil infrastructure projects.
•	Repair and maintain existing brick, cement block, and related masonry structures on site.
•	Comply with all Monolith Civil Australia Work Health and Safety (WHS) policies and procedures.
•	Erect and dismantle scaffolding safely to facilitate masonry work at heights.
•	Identify and report site hazards, near misses, and incidents to the Site Supervisor immediately.
•	Ensure all masonry work complies with the Building Code of Australia (BCA) and relevant structural engineering standards.

Essential Skills

•	Advanced ability to read and interpret complex civil construction plans and structural diagrams.
•	Strong spatial awareness and ability to calculate material quantities accurately.
•	High level of physical fitness and stamina to perform manual labour, lift heavy materials, and work in various weather conditions.
•	Exceptional precision in alignment, leveling, and finishing of masonry structures.

Finance Manager  
 Northern Beaches, New South Wales 
   About the Organisation  
 This position sits within a premier, long established commercial precinct located on Sydney's Northern Beaches. Managing a substantial commercial footprint with 94 staff, 1,800 active members, and multi use facilities, the business offers a dynamic, high volume operational environment. The organisation prides itself on delivering high quality service to its members while maintaining strong financial sustainability, robust governance, and long term strategic planning. 
   Role Description  
 Reporting directly to the General Manager, this is the lead finance seat for the business. You will hold full ownership of the financial, accounting, and operational governance functions. Leading an established team of four direct reports, you will provide clear direction and day to day management while ensuring total integrity of all financial records and compliance standards. 
 The role centers heavily on hands on financial management, budgeting, cash flow forecasting, and senior stakeholder engagement. A core requirement is the ability to translate complex financial data into clear commentary and confidently present these insights directly to the General Manager and the Board of Directors. 
 This is a permanent, full time position requiring five days on site on the Northern Beaches, with flexibility required to attend periodic evening Board or Committee meetings. The role offers a competitive salary package of $130,000 to $145,000 + Super, plus an annual performance bonus scheme and standard leave entitlements. 
   Key Responsibilities  
 
 
  Financial Management and Reporting : Manage complete day to day financial operations. Prepare accurate monthly management accounts including P&L statements, Balance Sheets, Cash Flow statements, and key financial performance indicators. 
 
 
  Board and Stakeholder Communication : Prepare, present, and communicate comprehensive financial reports, scenario modelling, and commentary directly to Management and the Board of Directors. 
 
 
  Team Leadership : Provide day to day management, direction, and support to an experienced team of four covering Accounts Payable, Payroll, Membership, and Reception. 
 
 
  Budgeting and Forecasting : Coordinate the annual budgeting process across all operational departments, monitor performance against budget, and deliver accurate cash flow projections. 
 
 
  Statutory Compliance and Audit : Oversee end to end accounting operations, coordinate annual financial statement preparation in accordance with Australian Accounting Standards, and act as the primary liaison for external auditors. 
 
 
  Commercial Asset Oversight : Maintain oversight of treasury, fixed asset registers, capital expenditure, purchasing frameworks, and inventory stocktakes. 
 
 
  Systems and IT Oversight : Act as the primary liaison for external IT providers and support a software migration project on the horizon over the next 12 months. 
 
 
   Qualifications and Skills  
 
 
 A Bachelor's degree in Commerce, Finance, Accounting, or a related discipline. 
 
 
 Professional accounting qualification (CA, CPA, or working towards) is preferred. 
 
 
 5 plus years of experience in a senior financial management or hands on accounting role. 
 
 
 Proven people management skills with the confidence to lead a strong, long tenured, and established team. 
 
 
 Exceptional communication skills, with demonstrated experience presenting complex financial data clearly to non-financial managers and Board members. 
 
 
 Background in hospitality is highly desirable. 
 
 
 Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, point of sale (POS), and database reporting. 
 
 
   What's on Offer?  
 
 
 Lead finance seat within a well regarded Northern Beaches organisation. 
 
 
 High visibility role with direct exposure to executive management and the Board of Directors. 
 
 
 An attractive remuneration package of $130,000 to $145,000 + Super + Annual Performance Bonus. 
 
 
 On-site parking and scenic Northern Beaches workplace setting. 
 
 
  If you are a hands on, execution focused finance leader with strong team management and board reporting experience, apply now.

Buterin L’Estrange Projects is proudly based in West Gosford, NSW, delivering exceptional outcomes across the commercial construction sector. Specialising in commercial construction, adaptive re-use projects, and premium retail fit-outs, we combine over 50 years of industry expertise with a modern, innovative, and agile approach to project delivery.

Our team is committed to creating high-quality spaces through smart solutions, strong partnerships, and a hands-on approach that ensures every project is delivered with precision, efficiency, and attention to detail.

We are currently searching for a Mechanical Engineer to join our growing team.

The Mechanical Engineer is responsible for the design, engineering, documentation and technical coordination of projects from concept through to manufacture and installation. This role supports the successful delivery of commercial, retail, hospitality and bespoke joinery projects by producing accurate engineering designs, detailed shop drawings, CNC files, material schedules and technical documentation.

The Mechanical Engineer works closely with project managers, estimators, production staff, suppliers and clients to ensure projects are delivered safely, efficiently, on time and within budget.

Key responsibilities include

Engineering & Design:
- Prepare mechanical designs for commercial joinery and bespoke products.
- Produce detailed manufacturing drawings using AutoCAD and SolidWorks.
- Develop 2D and 3D models for client presentation and manufacturing.
- Review architectural drawings and specifications.
- Ensure all designs comply with relevant Australian Standards and project requirements.
- Resolve technical design issues throughout the project lifecycle.

Manufacturing Support:
- Prepare fabrication and shop drawings for production.
- Produce CNC machining files.
- Generate Bills of Materials (BOM).
- Generate Bills of Quantities (BOQ).
- Coordinate design changes with production staff.
- Provide technical support to the workshop during manufacture.

Project Coordination:
- Assist Project Managers with technical planning.
- Coordinate with architects, consultants and clients regarding design requirements.
- Monitor engineering progress to meet project deadlines.
- Assist with prototype development where required.
- Participate in project meetings.

Estimating Support:
- Complete quantity take-offs from tender documentation;
- Assist with material selection;
- Review engineering requirements during tender preparation;
- Provide technical advice during estimating.

Quality & Continuous Improvement:
- Ensure drawings are accurate before release.
- Maintain document control.
- Identify opportunities to improve manufacturing efficiency.
- Assist in reducing production errors and rework.

Health, Safety & Compliance:
- Comply with WHS legislation and company policies.
- Ensure engineering designs consider safe manufacture and installation.
- Follow company quality management procedures.
- Participate in toolbox meetings and safety initiatives.

To be considered you will need a relevant Bachelor Degree and at least 1 year of related employment experience.

This is a full time position, an immediate start is available. A remuneration package of $80,000 - $90,000 per annum will be offered to the successful candidate.
